questions.question: Who was the first social reformer to view modern education as a vehicle for the spread of modern ideas in the country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• He believed that education could play a crucial role in the development of the **country and the upliftment of its people.**
 
• He established the **Hindu College in Calcutta in 1817, **which later became the nucleus of the **University of Calcutta.**
 
• He also advocated for the** education of women and girls,** and supported the idea of** English education.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Savitribai Phule** was also a **social reformer** who worked for the **education of girls and women,** and established the **first school for girls** in India.
 
• **Swami Vivekananda **was a **spiritual leader and philosopher** who emphasized the importance of **education f**or the development of the individual and the nation.
 
• Hence, the **correct **answer is option 1, Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

questions.question: The Moplah Uprising, an organised opposition of Muslim cultivators, occurred in which modern state of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Moplah Uprising, also known as the Mappila Rebellion, occurred in the Malabar region of Kerala in 1921.
 
• This rebellion was led by the Mappila Muslims of Kerala, who were primarily tenants and cultivators.
 
• The uprising was a reaction against British colonial rule and the oppressive practices of landlords.
 
• The rebellion saw widespread violence and was one of the significant peasant movements in the Indian independence struggle.
 
• It was part of the larger Khilafat Movement and Non-Cooperation Movement against British rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khilafat Movement:**

 
 
• A pan-Islamist political campaign launched by Muslims in British India to influence the British government not to abolish the Ottoman Caliphate.
 
• It was led by prominent Muslim leaders like Maulana Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:**
 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, this was a mass protest against British rule.
 
• It aimed at inducing the British government to grant self-governance to India.
 
 
 
• **Malabar Region:**
 
 
• Located in the northern part of Kerala, the Malabar region was historically significant due to its trading ports.
 
• It was a major center for the spice trade and saw various foreign influences over centuries.
 
 
 
• **Tenant Farming:**
 
 
• A system where farmers cultivate land owned by another and pay rent in the form of cash or a portion of the produce.
 
• In the Malabar region, the oppressive practices by landlords led to widespread discontent among tenant farmers.

With reference to the ‘Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO)’, consider the following statements: 

1. It is an oceanic-atmospheric phenomenon which affects weather activities most prominent over the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

** Madden-Julian Oscillation:**

 
• The Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO), as it’s called, is a **moving band of rain clouds** that travels around the globe-spanning 12,000–20,000 km across the tropical oceans. 
 
• There can be multiple MJO events within a season, and so the **MJO is best described as intra-seasonal tropical climate variability.**
 
• The surface and upper-atmosphere structure of the MJO for a period when the enhanced convective phase (thunderstorm cloud) is centred across the **Indian Ocean** and the suppressed convective phase is centred over the **west-central Pacific Ocean.**
 
• The entire system shifts eastward over time, eventually circling the globe and returning to its point of origin. 
 
• **Thus, It is an oceanic-atmospheric phenomenon which affects weather activities most prominent over the Indian and Pacific Oceans.* Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Effects of MJO on global weather phenomenon:**
 
 
• The presence of Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) over the Pacific Ocean along with an El Nino is detrimental to Monsoon rains. It can modulate the timing and strength of monsoons.* Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• It **Influences tropical cyclone** **numbers **and **strength **in nearly all ocean basins.
 
• It can result in** jet stream changes** that can lead to cold air outbreaks, extreme heat events, and flooding rains over the United States and North America.

questions.question: Which of the following forest ecosystems in India is specifically characterized by arid conditions and is structurally dominated by plant species such as Babool and Cactus?

• Tropical Thorn Forests: These are arid Indian ecosystems located primarily in regions such as Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Haryana.
 
• Dominant Species: The vegetation in these forests is structurally dominated by xerophytic species like Babool and various types of Cacti, which are adapted to survive in low-moisture environments.
 
• Environmental Conditions: They are found in areas receiving very low rainfall, represented by a bright sun and cactus icon in climatic classifications, indicating high dryness and temperature.
 
• Comparison with other types: Unlike Tropical Evergreen forests which require heavy rainfall, Thorn forests thrive in water-scarce zones of the Indian subcontinent.

• Montane Forests: Located in high-altitude regions like the Himalayas (e.g., Pine, Deodar).
 
• Mangrove Forests: Coastal ecosystems found in deltas like the Sundarbans.
 
 
 
• The distribution of these biomes is primarily governed by the gradient of temperature and dryness.
